Atul Kumar Dubey And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
on 29 May, 2025

Author: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
Bench: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Petitioner :- Pradeep Pandey,Prashant Pandey

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Anil Kumar-X,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. Although, the prayer made in this writ petition is to quash the FIR dated 05.01.2025 registered as Case Crime No.4 of 2025 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 427 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.
Nandganj, Distt. Ghazipur, but when the matter has been taken up, learned counsel for the Atul Kumar Dubey And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115660917/
1 petitioners has submitted that the directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Md. Asfak Alam v. State of Jharkhand (2023) 7 SCC 69, as well as the recent directives in Criminal Appeal No(s). 2207 of 2023 arising out of Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 3433 of 2023, passed on 31.07.2023, clearly stipulate the procedural safeguards to be followed before arresting an accused.

sentences.text: These directions emphasize that arrest should not be made automatically, and police officers must ensure compliance with Section 41 CrPC before any arrest is made.

Specifically, the circular issued by the Director General of Police, Uttar Pradesh (DGP Circular No. 31/2023 dated 17.08.2023) mandates that these guidelines be strictly followed by police officers, ensuring that arrests are made only after adequate justification and review.
Despite these clear legal requirements, the investigating officer in this case has failed to follow due process and is threatening the petitioners with arrest, in violation of these principles.

3. We have perused the FIR, which prima facie discloses cognizable offences against the petitioners and therefore, the prayer made to quash the FIR cannot be entertained in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017)
2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2021) SCC Online SC 315 and as such, we are of the view that no interference is warranted.

sentences.text:
4. However, considering the fact that all the offences, complained of in the impugned FIR, are punishable with a term up to seven years, therefore, in case of effecting the arrest of the petitioners in pursuance of the impugned FIR, it is directed that the respondents/ authorities shall ensure that the specific provisions contained in Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of CrPC/Section 35(3) to 35(7)
of Bhartiya Nagrika Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (Supra) as well as the directions issued in judgement and order dated 28.01.2021 of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 17732 of 2020 (Vimal Kumar and 3 Others Vs. State of U.P. and 3 Others) reported in 2021 (2) ACR 1147, be strictly complied with.
5.
